sentences.text:
Mihir Naskar vs Unknown on 1 December, 2025
94. 01.12.2025
Court
No.8 (Tanmoy)
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Ia No: Cran/2/2025

In
 Cra (Db)/179/2025
 In Re: - An application under Section 389(1) of Cr.PC,
 1973/430(1) of Bnss, 2023 in connection with the judgment
 and order dated 27.01.2025, passed by the learned Additional
 District & Sessions Judge, 16th Court, Alipore, South 24-
 Parganas in St No.04(07) 2014 under Section 376/506 of the
 Indian Penal Code, 1860.

And
 In the matter of: - Mihir Naskar
 ...applicant/appellant.
 Mr. Debajyoti Deb
 Ms. Somdyuti Parekh
 Mr. H.K. Jha
 ...for the applicant/appellant.

Ms. Amita Gaur, Sr. Govt. Adv.
 Ms. Ayana De
 ...for the Stat
 Mr. Atanu Das
 ...for the de facto complainant.
Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.

1. The applicant/appellant was convicted by the learned Trial Court under Sections 376/506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 by judgment and order dated 27/31.01.2025, passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, 16th Court, Alipore, South 24-Parganas in ST No.04(07) 2014,
and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight (08) years apart from being fined for a sum of Rs.10,000/-.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Judge, 16th Court, Alipore, South 24-Parganas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The applicant/appellant says that he has been framed.
The complaint was lodged by the victim girl seven years after the incident.
Even the evidence on record does not support the prosecution case.
There was a relationship between the victim and the applicant.
The belated complaint is clearly to frame the applicant for ulterior motive.
The applicant prays for suspension of sentence pending disposal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Learned State Counsel and learned Counsel for the de facto complainant strongly oppose the prayer.
They say that out of fear the victim girl did not lodge complaint contemporaneously with the incident.
It has been confirmed that the child to whom the victim girl gave birth four months after her arranged marriage, is the child of the applicant/appellant.
The DNA test has confirmed this.
No leniency should be shown to such a person.
4. Further, the applicant has criminal antecedents.

Apart from the present case, Gosaba Police Station Case No. 59/2011 dated 05/06/2011, under Sections 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860,
is pending against the applicant.
5. In reply, learned Advocate for the applicant says that Gosaba Police Station Case No. 59/2011 dated 05/06/2011 is a politically motivated case.
There were forty persons who have been charge-sheeted in that case.
The applicant was granted bail on the very first day and is still on bail.

6. Let the report dated December 1, 2025, signed by the Officer-in-Charge of Gosaba Police Station,
Baruipur Police District, filed in Court today be kept with the records.
7.

entities.text:
Gosaba Police Station,
Baruipur Police District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: We have considered the facts and circumstances of the case.

On a prima facie assimilation of the material on record and considering that even in the present case, the applicant was all throughout on bail during the trial and it is nobodys case that he misused the privilege of bail or breached any condition thereof, we are inclined to allow this application and we hereby do suspend the sentence of imprisonment of the present applicant/appellant.
8.

It is thus ORDERED that the applicant, namely, MIHIR NASKAR shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, South 24-Parganas at Alipore, subject to condition that the applicant shall remain within the geographical limits of the district of South 24-Parganas but shall not enter the territorial jurisdiction of Gosaba Police Station and shall furnish his present address to the Inspector-in- Charge/Officer-in-Charge of the concerned Police Station within whose jurisdiction he shall be presently residing and shall meet such Inspector-in-Charge/Officer-in-Charge of the jurisdictional Police Station where he will be presently residing, once every fortnight until further orders and that the applicant/appellant shall be personally present or be represented before this Court on each and every date when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
9. The operation of the order of conviction and sentence shall remain suspended till disposal of the appeal or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
We also stay the operation of payment of fine till disposal of the appeal.

10. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

2 11.

We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
12. The application being IA No: CRAN/2/2025 is accordingly disposed of.

13. We find from the judgment and order of the learned Trial Court that there was a direction on the District Legal Services Authority (in short DLSA), South 24-Parganas to monitor and expedite the disbursement of compensation amount of Rs.8 lakh to the victim girl of this case.
14. Learned Advocate for the victim girl says that she has not received any money till now.

15. The Member-Secretary, DLSA, South 24-Parganas is directed to file a report before us through the learned Registrar (Judicial Service) of this Court as to why the compensation amount has still not been paid to the victim girl.

Such report will be placed before us two weeks hence (15.12.2025),
when this matter will be listed again under the heading "To Be Mentioned".
16.
This order shall be communicated by the Registry of this Court as well as learned Counsel for the State to the Member-Secretary of DLSA, South 24-Parganas forthwith.

We find from a departmental note dated November 12, 2025 that the Trial Court Records (TCRs)
have been received by the department and the same are awaiting examination.
The department shall expedite the process of preparation and filing of paper books by the end of January, 2026.

18. Let the appeal appear under the appropriate heading in the Combined Monthly list of February,
2026.
19.
Criminal Section is directed to make available certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance with all requisite formalities.
(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.)

(Arijit Banerjee,
J.)
